A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BPO study. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and relocated or renamed material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original dialogue-generation, summarization and instruction-following experiments, including BPO benchmark results, ablations and generated examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports BPO results using Llama-3-8B-Base in Table 6.

M1.justification: The BPO objective, SBA scaling, model-ratio formulations and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Newly specified loss-mixture weights document implementation choices without establishing a revision to the method used for retained results.

E1.justification: Coverage remains Anthropic-HH dialogue, TL;DR summarization, UltraFeedback-based alignment, and AlpacaEval2/Arena-Hard evaluation. The added Llama-3-8B-Base experiment changes the model configuration within retained tasks, rather than introducing a new dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: Table 6 removes the Llama-3-8B-Instruct comparisons against SimPO-v1 and f-PO, retaining SimPO-v2 under the name SimPO. f-PO remains evaluated elsewhere. The Mistral comparator set was already present in v1 Appendix Table 8; the new Llama-Base block uses the retained comparator set.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluation of Llama-3-8B-Base, with a SimPO model ratio, lambda = -0.5, ratio clipping to [0.01, 30], and equal SBA/logistic-loss weights. Existing benchmark sizes, judges, metrics and retained experimental protocols remain unchanged. Newly disclosed mixture weights for existing experiments do not establish that their settings changed.

E4.justification: The lambda and temperature sweeps, compatibility experiments, gradient-scaling analysis and generated examples are retained, including Figures 5–10 and Appendix D. The added backbone benchmark is not a new ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: The new checklist states that computational limits prevented error bars and repeated-run statistical tests. This conflicts with the unchanged standard deviations and confidence intervals in Appendix D.2, Figure 9 and Table 8. Thus reporting changes, but no changed run count, seed information or uncertainty-estimation procedure is established.

E6.justification: Table 6 adds Llama-3-8B-Base results: BPO scores 22.5% AlpacaEval LC, 18.7% raw win rate and 31.7% Arena-Hard win rate; its raw win rate is below SimPO's 20.3%. SimPO-v1/f-PO result entries are removed. Most Mistral entries reproduce v1 Table 8, but newly displayed Arena-Hard values disagree with that retained table: RRHF 5.8 versus 6.9, CPO 6.9 versus 5.8, and R-DPO 8.0 versus 9.9. Other principal results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The assumptions, propositions, theorems and Appendix A–B derivations are retained. The explicit DPO-recovery calculation added to Section 3.3 already appeared in v1 Appendix A.5, so it adds explanation rather than new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims: tractable optimality-preserving ratio matching, DPO as a special case, SBA gradient scaling, compatibility with other objectives, and 55.9% AlpacaEval2 length-controlled win rate.

C2.justification: The new checklist explicitly acknowledges limited computational resources and presents consistency across models, datasets and ablations as support in place of repeated-run statistical tests. This adds a qualification about evidential support; the existing mechanism explanations and Section 6 applicability limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 now specifies SBA/logistic-loss weights of 0.3/0.7 for Mistral and 0.05/0.95 for Llama-3-8B-Instruct, and documents the added Llama-Base configuration. The abstract adds a project-code link, and the checklist adds code/checkpoint release statements. These improve documentation without establishing external resource availability.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds MPO and a paragraph connecting likelihood-ratio estimation to GANs, VAEs, diffusion models and concurrent concrete-score distillation work, with corresponding citation additions. The central positioning against f-DPO and f-PO remains unchanged; DDRO was already discussed in v1 Appendix B.4.

P1.justification: v2 expands the explanation of DPO recovery, rewrites the benchmark-results paragraph, adds related-work discussion, acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist, and standardizes terminology and cross-references. Most existing prose and the main section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Table 6 changes from a narrow single-backbone display to a full-width table with three backbone groups. Several existing tables and figures move with the text, appendix tables receive small spacing changes, and Table 5's TL;DR caption is corrected. The figure graphics themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Explicit loss-mixture weights resolve a concrete reproducibility omission, while the added Llama-3-8B-Base comparison supplies limited additional validation. These gains modestly improve the paper, but new Table 6/Table 8 baseline discrepancies and the checklist's contradictory error-bar statement weaken reporting consistency. The method, proofs and headline results remain unchanged, so the improvement is limited.
